- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent volatility, then forecasts back toward historical mean too aggressively.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model often misses early downward turns, especially after sentiment shifts from positive to neutral/negative.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.8–0.9), model tends to overpredict price increases; when sentiment is falling (e.g., 0.1–0.3), it underpredicts drops.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment shifts often invalidate 30d forecasts unless anchored to recent sentiment reversal.
- If sentiment is stable or flat (0.3–0.7), model should not overfit to recent price movements — use smoother trend filters.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high, model should not forecast higher than 1.2x recent peak unless confirmed by technical confirmation (e.g., volume, volatility).
